question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $13,$ the additive inverse of $-50$ modulo $13$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $-50$ modulo $13$ is the integer $0\le x<13$ such that

$$
x+(-50)≡0\,(\text{mod}\,13).
$$

First, we note that $-50≡2\,(\text{mod}\,13):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}-50 & ≡(-4)\cdot 13+2 & \,(\text{mod}\,13) \\  & ≡(-4)\cdot 0+2 & \,(\text{mod}\,13) \\  & ≡2 & \,(\text{mod}\,13)\end{aligned}
$$

Also, note that $-2+2≡0,$ so $x≡-2\,(\text{mod}\,13).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-2 & \,(\text{mod}\,13) \\  & ≡0-2 & \,(\text{mod}\,13) \\  & ≡13-2 & \,(\text{mod}\,13) \\  & ≡11 & \,(\text{mod}\,13)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $-50$ modulo $13$ is $11.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-50+11≡-39≡(-3)\cdot 13≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,13)\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
